title: Top Row: E and I
summary: Reach up to E and I from home and come back, without lifting your whole hand.

explain.goal: Reach E and I on the top row with your middle fingers, then return home.
why: The top row is one short step up from home. If you move only the finger, your other fingers stay on the home row and keep their bearings.
Returning to home after each reach is what lets you find keys by feel. Without it, every reach becomes a small search.
Moving your whole hand instead of one finger is slower and loses your place, so the habit worth building is finger only.
how: Left middle finger reaches up from D to E. Right middle finger reaches up from K to I.
Keep the other fingers resting on their home keys.
Press, then bring the finger straight back down to D or K.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting your whole hand to reach the top row
mistakes.reason: Your other fingers leave home, so the next key is a guess.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the finger up after the press
mistakes.reason: If it does not return, the next home-row key has to be found again.

explain.recap: Reach with one finger, press, and go straight back home. The rest of your hand stays put.

title: Top Row: R and U
summary: Add R and U with your index fingers, which already own that column, so the reach feels natural.

explain.goal: Reach R with your left index finger and U with your right index finger.
why: R and U sit just above F and J. Your index fingers already own those columns, so the reach is short.
These are common letters, so learning them early makes real words possible.
how: Left index finger reaches up from F to R. Right index finger reaches up from J to U.
Return to F or J straight after the press.

mistakes.mistake: Reaching for R or U with a middle finger
mistakes.reason: They belong to the index fingers. Using another finger breaks the map you are learning.
A small finger movement is enough, and twisting throws your hand off home.

explain.recap: R and U belong to your index fingers. Reach, press, and come back to F and J.

title: Top Row: W and O
summary: Add W and O with your ring fingers, and practice slowly since these fingers are less independent.

explain.goal: Reach W with your left ring finger and O with your right ring finger.
why: Ring fingers are less independent, so the reach up to W and O can feel awkward at first.
Slow, accurate practice trains them. Speed comes once they hit the right key every time.
how: Left ring finger reaches up from S to W. Right ring finger reaches up from L to O.
Keep the rest of your hand relaxed and on home.

mistakes.mistake: Rushing and hitting the neighboring key
mistakes.reason: A wrong key needs a correction, which costs more time than a slow, accurate press.
Tension slows the other fingers too. Stay loose and move one finger.

explain.recap: W and O belong to the ring fingers. Go slowly, stay relaxed, and return to S and L.

title: Top Row: Q, T, Y, P
summary: Add Q, T, Y, and P, the edge keys of the top row, each with the finger that owns it.

explain.goal: Type Q, T, Y, and P with the correct finger each time.
why: These four sit at the edges of the top row, so they are the longest reaches. Getting them right keeps the rest of your hand steady.
T and Y belong to your index fingers, which cover two columns. Q and P belong to your pinkies.
how: Left pinky reaches up from A to Q. Right pinky reaches up from ; to P.
Left index finger reaches T. Right index finger reaches Y.
Return to the home key after each press.

mistakes.mistake: Stretching a stronger finger sideways to reach Q or P
mistakes.reason: It looks like a shortcut, but it pulls that finger off its own keys.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing T or Y with a middle finger
mistakes.reason: Both belong to the index fingers, which cover two columns each.

explain.recap: Q and P belong to your pinkies, T and Y to your index fingers. Reach, press, and return.

title: Top Row: Full Words
summary: Type real words from the whole top row, so the reaches become a smooth habit.

explain.goal: Type real words that mix home row and top row keys.
why: Now you will use the whole top row. In real words, fingers reach up and come back down constantly.
This is where home-row return pays off, because every reach is followed by a quick return.
how: Use the finger that owns each key, and let it return to home after each reach.
Keep your eyes on the text, not on your fingers.

mistakes.mistake: Hunting for a key you have not learned yet
mistakes.reason: Stop and check the keyboard guide if you are unsure, then go back to typing by feel.

mistakes.mistake: Going faster than your accuracy allows
mistakes.reason: Accuracy is what the pass mark checks, and mistakes cost more time than a steady pace.

explain.recap: Reach up with one finger, come back to home, and keep your eyes on the words.
